en: The Banaue Rice Terraces act as giant inclined planes, reducing the effort needed for farmers to carry crops up the steep Cordillera mountains.
The microscopic hairs on a Philippine tarsier's feet increase surface friction, allowing the small primate to grip tree branches tightly without slipping.
The Diwata-2 microsatellite orbits Earth in continuous freefall, experiencing microgravity while moving at a high velocity of roughly 27,000 kilometers per hour.
Camarines Norte contains large deposits of magnetite, a naturally magnetic iron ore that can attract small iron objects like paperclips without external electricity.
The Binga Hydroelectric Plant in Benguet generates electricity by using flowing water to spin large turbines connected to electrical generators.
Fireflies along Bohol's Loboc River produce cold bioluminescent light through a chemical reaction inside their abdomens, without generating excess heat.
Traditional Kalinga gangsa flat gongs produce distinct musical sounds when their bronze surfaces vibrate after being struck by padded wooden sticks.
The Tiwi Geothermal Power Plant in Albay generates electricity by harnessing thermal energy from hot underground steam to spin turbines.
The massive concrete wall of the Magat Dam in Isabela holds back water to store immense gravitational potential energy.
The traditional Ilocano bolo acts as a wedge, concentrating force onto a thin, sharp edge to split coconuts and cut thick vines.
Rubbing dry Philippine narra wood sticks together generates heat through friction, eventually creating enough thermal energy to ignite a small fire.
Junk shops in Divisoria use giant electromagnets, which require an electrical current to generate the magnetic force needed to lift heavy steel.
